name: thin-job
about: An opening with one fact and no description: few honest angles exist.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Drivers who hold a CDL, are driving now and compare openings by what the job pays per week. A plain pay amount stated up front would make them stop. This carrier has no ad history yet, so this rests on the job's facts alone.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per week, stated plainly, for a CDL driver opening.
angles.proof: The job states what the opening pays per week.
angles.why: Pay is the only concrete fact the job gives, so it carries the ad. Nothing has been measured for this carrier yet, so this is a starting point, not a proven winner.

angles.idea: Lead with what knowing the pay per week means for planning life at home, without promising any time at home.
angles.proof: The job states the pay as an amount per week.
angles.why: The job gives no fact about time at home, so this angle rests on the pay per week alone. Nothing has been measured, so it tests whether a home framing draws CDL drivers.

angles.idea: Lead with the truck waiting for a CDL driver, then state the pay per week; claim nothing about make, age or features.
angles.proof: The opening is for a CDL driver and states what it pays per week.
angles.why: The job has no equipment fact, so the picture carries the hook and the pay carries the claim. Untested; the benchmark's pause point says when to stop it.
